rows.name: spoken-why-warps-frozen-5
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Because threads in a warp share instruction execution, different branches can require separate execution paths with only some threads active, reducing efficiency. Similar control flow keeps more threads doing useful work together. Accessing consecutive memory locations also lets the GPU combine memory requests into fewer transactions, improving memory throughput.

rows.name: spoken-why-during-coding-frozen-21
rows.question: Why?
rows.answer: Interpreting “Y” as “why”: a circular array gives the FIFO exactly 17 slots and constant-time push and pop without shifting elements. Tracking the head and current size distinguishes empty from full, so all 17 slots are usable and overflow can be rejected without changing existing contents. Advancing indices modulo 17 reuses freed slots while preserving FIFO order.
